items.title: George "Pops" Foster and Mugsy Spanier Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: The interviewee does not speak about Mugsy Spanier in the first person; the interviewer mentions 'Mugzi' and discusses being in the band, while the interviewee only comments on the recording quality ('They're supposed to be the most perfectly recorded jazz band. They sure sound good.')

ctx.x: A string bass is a rhythm. Mugzi had the right idea. But you got to do it. Now they want you to do it. I just like to get back there and just play some rhythm and let the melody instruments out there play. Just play them some string rhythm and let them go.

My brother and dad would drive to New York just to hear a band or we can go back. Back to school. Well, we used to rehearse at least twice a week. We'd leave in rehearsal and the band sounded like it too. Well, it showed it too. So I would get an idea. We'd drop out of our own arrangements. They'd have to put them down. Solos records will sound good always. They still sound good and they'll sound good 50 years from now.
